title: The Twilio auth token, her address and her medication list sit in a world-readable file
method: end-to-end run of `cura setup` then `cura add-phone` against a throwaway HOME, then stat(2) on everything written

must_not_contain: readable by other accounts and by every
it should be 0700. Every other account

observed_at_discovery: Ran the real wizard.run() and add_phone.run() with a scripted HOME. Afterwards: ~/.cura is 0775, ~/.cura/setup-progress.json is 0664, ~/.cura/margaret.json is 0600. setup-progress.json contains "twilio_sid", "twilio_token" (the full 32-hex Auth Token), "twilio_number", the resident's phone, the caregiver's phone, "meds": "Lisinopril, Metformin" and "address": "412 County Road 14, Buffalo, Wyoming". add_phone.py chmods only the derived config, with the comment '# the auth token lives here now'; the token lives in two files and only one is locked. Under a normal umask of 022 the modes are 0755/0644 rather than 0775/0664 -- still world-readable either way. pytest exit 1, 2 failed.
